result.policy:
SOP-PH-07 Medicine recalls
1. On receipt of a recall notice, identify every location holding an affected lot: the central store and all ward automated cabinets. Ward cabinets record products and quantities but not batch numbers. The central store issue log shows which batches were sent to which cabinet and when; a pharmacist can also inspect a cabinet on site.
2. Quarantine all affected stock the same shift. Quarantining at a ward cabinet means a pharmacist goes to the ward and removes the batch. Quarantined stock is collected by the wholesaler; do not dispose of it.
3. Only the lot numbers named in the notice are affected. Do not withdraw other lots of the same product.
4. Withdrawing stock must not leave a ward without a critical medicine: arrange replacement supply (transfer, urgent order, or an approved alternative) before the next round.
5. Recheck affected lots on following shifts until all have been withdrawn.

SOP-PH-18 Cold chain
Refrigerated medicines are kept at 2-8 C in the medication refrigerator at each location. After a temperature alarm or any reading outside 2-8 C, review that refrigerator's temperature log and assess each refrigerated batch it held against the stability guidance in get_drug_info: the highest temperature reached, whether it froze, and the batch's cumulative time outside 2-8 C (earlier time is in the batch record, get_lot_record; add the hours of this excursion). Withdraw (quarantine) batches that fail the guidance; batches that pass stay in use. Stock of a failed batch that has been moved on from that refrigerator since the excursion began (see get_issue_log) is affected too and must be withdrawn where it now is. Then arrange replacement supply.

SOP-PH-11 Medicine shortages
Ward cabinets are restocked automatically from the central store at the end of each shift (to par level) and the central store receives routine wholesaler deliveries every second day. When routine supply is interrupted, the on-duty pharmacist may transfer stock between locations, place urgent orders with RapidRx Express (delivered at the start of the next shift, 40% surcharge), or approve a formulary alternative for a ward. Allocation priority under policy P-12: ICU and ED first, then other wards.

SOP-PH-12 Therapeutic substitution
Only alternatives on the P&T Committee formulary list F-3 may be approved. A ward-level approval lets the ward cabinet issue the alternative to any patient on that ward when the original product is out of stock. Some alternatives carry a restriction (for example a contraindication in a drug allergy): these must not be approved ward-wide while any patient on the ward has that allergy; approve them for individual patients after checking the patient list. Use get_drug_info to see approved alternatives and restrictions, and list_patients to see patients and allergies.

SOP-PH-16 Ward requests for extra stock
Ward cabinets are restocked to par automatically. A request for stock above par should be checked against the ward's recent usage and current cabinet stock before it is met: meet requests that the data support, and do not move scarce stock to a ward that does not need it, because it is then unavailable to other wards. Stock can be transferred back.

SOP-PH-14 Urgent orders
Urgent orders go to RapidRx Express, arrive at the central store at the start of the next shift and cost list price plus 40%. Order what is needed to bridge the gap; overstock ties up budget.
